rows.title: Test-Time Training for Speech Enhancement
rows.semantic_reasoning: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate speech-prior-denoising within noise-enhancement.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: An enhancement model should adapt when the noise at test time differs from training, even without labeled examples from the new environment. Mechanism: The main enhancement task shares representations with an auxiliary task optimized on the current noisy signal, with strategies trading adaptation gain against test-time cost. Result: The paper reports consistent speech-quality improvements over its baseline on synthetic and real-world datasets. Boundary: The adaptation steps, compute budget, noise conditions, and author-reported metrics bound the result; listener benefit and long-term stability remain open.

rows.title: Pitfalls and Limits in Automatic Dementia Assessment
rows.semantic_reasoning: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate clinical-speech-marker within clinical-and-assistive-speech.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A speech-based dementia score can correlate with human scores while still being systematically wrong for some people. Mechanism: The analysis links scoring artifacts to speech production decline, ASR errors, and fallback handling; apparent agreement can therefore arise from the test design. Result: The paper reports high overall correlation but weaker behavior for healthy and mildly impaired groups and identifies overoptimistic correlations for severely impaired speakers. Boundary: This is an analysis of one standardized assessment and its data; it warns against clinical claims, not a universal ranking of dementia-screening systems.

rows.title: Non-Standard Accent TTS Support via Large Multi-Accent Frontend Pronunciation Knowledge Transfer
rows.semantic_reasoning: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate text-to-speech-planning within text-to-speech-and-content.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A text-to-speech system should pronounce an accent it has barely seen without requiring a large new pronunciation database. Mechanism: The frontend predicts phones, lexical stress, and prosodic boundaries; target accents are trained with reduced data and compared with full-data and single-accent baselines. Result: The paper reports up to 95% less pronunciation training data for robust performance and examines 14 English accents using LibriTTS and HiFi-TTS-derived data. Boundary: Accuracy is reported for the studied accents, frontend labels, and datasets; transfer to other languages, voices, and synthesis backends remains unestablished.

rows.title: NGPU-LM: GPU-Accelerated N-Gram Language Model for Context-Biasing in Greedy ASR Decoding
rows.semantic_reasoning: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate domain-and-context-biasing within adaptation-and-open-vocabulary.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A recognizer must recognize rare or domain-specific words without paying the full cost of beam search on every utterance. Mechanism: NGPU-LM uses hash-based transition lookup and customizable greedy decoding so context biasing can recover domain words with less than 7% reported overhead. Result: The paper reports recovery of more than half the greedy/beam accuracy gap in out-of-domain tests and up to 10.6% relative WER improvement in its experiments. Boundary: The results depend on tested ASR architectures, domains, GPU implementation, and author-reported measurements; deployment energy and other hardware remain open.

rows.title: Intelligibility Prediction for Time-Modified Speech Signals Using Spectro-Temporal Modulation Features
rows.semantic_reasoning: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate word-error-versus-understanding within metrics-and-targets.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A speech-quality score should remain meaningful when processing changes the timing of the speech, not only its spectrum. Mechanism: The system uses DTW over modulation features and compares two ways of incorporating the alignment into RB-SIPAs across noise and time-modification conditions. Result: The paper reports better alignment behavior and better correlation with listening scores than MFCC-based alternatives under its tested conditions. Boundary: The listening datasets, degradation types, chosen modulation channels, and reference availability bound the claim; correlation is not a complete model of listener experience.

rows.title: Better Semi-supervised Learning for Multi-domain ASR Through Incremental Retraining and Data Filtering
rows.semantic_reasoning: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate self-training-and-pseudo-labels within low-resource-and-data-creation.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A recognizer needs to adapt to a new domain when only a little labeled speech is available but related audio is abundant. Mechanism: The pipeline retrains in stages and uses agreement or entity preservation to decide which generated transcripts enter the next training round. Result: The paper reports up to 22.3% relative improvement on Wow and 24.8% on Fisher over random selection, with consensus strongest and NER cheaper. Boundary: The gains are bounded to the two English corpora, model ensemble, filtering thresholds, and author-reported WER; other domains and languages remain unresolved.

rows.title: ASR-based segmentation for the analysis of larger child-speech datasets: Performance evaluation on vowels from Australian-English speaking children aged 4 to 11 years
rows.semantic_reasoning: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate alignment within boundaries-and-sequence-structure.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Large child-speech collections need segment boundaries, but an adult-trained aligner may place those boundaries according to a different rule than a human analyst. Mechanism: The study evaluates vowel boundaries in Australian-English child speech and asks how alignment error changes from ages four to eleven. Result: The paper reports that MFA falls short of human annotation, with smaller discrepancies for older children. Boundary: The evidence is tied to the tested vowels, ages, language variety, and annotators; it supports semi-automatic caution rather than universal aligner failure.

rows.title: Generalizable Audio Spoofing Detection using Non-Semantic Representations
rows.semantic_reasoning: The captured paper's ordinary problem, mechanism, and reported evaluation directly instantiate spoofing-and-deepfake within privacy-security-and-accountability.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A spoof detector should recognize synthetic audio from new generators and public-domain conditions, not only the generator seen during training. Mechanism: TRILL and TRILLsson representations are evaluated as features for a spoofing classifier across in-domain and public-domain conditions. Result: The paper reports comparable in-domain performance and stronger out-of-domain results than the tested baselines. Boundary: The generators, corpora, representation models, and author-reported tests define the boundary; future synthesis methods and adversarial adaptation remain open.
